card.name: Soran Bushi
card.era: Late 19th-early 20th century herring-fishing work song; modern Nanchu Soran dance from the early 1990s
card.tagline: Hokkaido herring-fishermen's sea shanty danced as net-hauling mime
card.profile: Soran Bushi is one of Japan's most famous min'yo (folk songs) and its associated dance, a sea shanty first sung by herring fishermen of Hokkaido to coordinate hauling nets (Wikipedia). The dance mimes pulling in fishing nets, the rolling waves and hauling the catch, punctuated by the call-and-response refrains 'Dokkoisho!' and 'Soran!', words used to encourage the fishermen's labor (Wikipedia). It emerged during the herring 'Golden Age' of the Meiji and Taisho eras (Reiroh). The widely known modern version, Nanchu Soran, was developed for Wakkanai Minami Junior High School and spread nationwide through schools (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Per Wikipedia, the Nanchu Soran choreography was developed by Butoh dancer Jusho Kasuga - acting out ocean waves, fishermen dragging nets, pulling ropes and lifting luggage over their shoulders - and the school won the Folk Song and Dance Awards honorable mention in 1992 and the Grand Prix of the Prime Minister of Japan in 1993 (Wikipedia).
